wildlife_and_plants.notes: The coast's cleverest camp thieves; reason hanging food is not allowed and canisters are required.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Comic mischief event; sketchable masked bandit.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Sea otter
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Kelp beds off Cape Alava and among the dense stacks south of the Arches; mothers carrying pups in summer 2026.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Journal sketch: otter floating on its back cracking a shell.

wildlife_and_plants.name: River otter
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Tracks on the sand every morning at several camps.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Harbor seal
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Hauls out on rocks in 'banana pose'; do not approach pups left on the beach.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Rule lesson: leave the pup alone.

wildlife_and_plants.name: California sea lion
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Barking from the offshore islands can be heard all night at Cape Alava.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Gray whale
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Migrates past in March-April and October (NPS); spouts seen off Alexander Island; many carcasses stranded in 2026.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Sketchable from a sunset camp; whale-carcass event.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Humpback whale
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Feeding offshore in summer; carcasses reported in 2026.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Bald eagle
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Common on snags above every camp.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Peregrine falcon
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Seen hunting shorebirds on the beach in Aug 2026.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Black oystercatcher
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Black shorebird with a bright red-orange bill on the intertidal rocks.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Easy colorful EGA sprite (black + light red).

wildlife_and_plants.name: Tufted puffin and common murre
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Nest on the offshore refuge islands (NPS); islands that cannot be walked to are off-limits.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Binocular sketch; rule lesson about refuges.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Great blue heron and belted kingfisher
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Fish the creek mouths and low-tide pools.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Purple shore crab
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Dozens scatter at every step on the rocky shelves, some rearing up with claws raised.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Tiny comic animation in tide-pool scenes.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Ochre sea star
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Orange and purple stars back in numbers after the wasting-disease years (2026 reports).

wildlife_and_plants.name: Giant green anemone
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Glowing green in low-tide pools.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Gooseneck barnacles and California mussels
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Crust the rocks; razor-sharp - why gloves matter.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Banana slug
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Yellow giants on the wet forest trails (many at Shi Shi, Aug 2026).
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Gentle comic encounter; yellow EGA sprite.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Cougar
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Sightings posted at Third Beach TH in June 2026.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Black-tailed deer
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Browse at the forest edge by the beach.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Sitka spruce
wildlife_and_plants.notes: The salt-tolerant giant of the coastal fringe; the Kalaloch Tree of Life is one.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Western redcedar
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Shreddy-barked cedars line the Ozette boardwalks (themselves made of cedar).

wildlife_and_plants.name: Shore pine
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Twisted small pines on bogs and windy points.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Salal
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Leathery shrub up to 8 ft along the Sand Point trail; hides cliff edges on overland trails; dark berries late summer.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Evergreen huckleberry and salmonberry
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Ripe berries along the trails in summer (2026 reports).

wildlife_and_plants.name: Skunk cabbage
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Bright yellow spathes in the spring mud of the overland trails.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Pacific rhododendron
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Pink blooms along the Ozette trails in late spring.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Licorice fern and sword fern
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Licorice fern on mossy branches; sword fern carpets the forest floor.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Bull kelp
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Offshore kelp forests where the otters live; wrack piles mark the high-tide line on the beach.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Teaching tool: read the wrack line before pitching a tent.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Sea palm
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Tiny palm-tree algae on surf-pounded rocks at very low tide.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Yellow sand verbena (possible)
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Golden-flowered dune plant of Pacific sandy beaches; presence on Olympic's wilderness beaches unverified.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Candidate coastal 'golden glow' to sketch at sunset - verify before using.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Old man's beard lichen (Usnea) and lungwort
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Hang from branches in the fog-soaked coastal forest.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Field-guide page; weather sign (wet = fog belt).

wildlife_and_plants.notes: Fall mushrooms in the coastal forest; shelf fungi on old logs.

permit_and_rules.rule: A wilderness camping permit is required for every overnight stay on the coast, year-round. Reserve on recreation.gov (Olympic Wilderness permit 4098362); no sites are held as walk-ups and paper trailhead self-registration is gone. Permits are issued ~3 days before the trip and can be self-printed.
Fees: $8 per adult (16+) per night, youth free, plus a $6 non-refundable reservation fee per permit; a $45 Annual Wilderness Pass covers nightly fees.

Ozette Coast quota area: camping from Yellow Banks to Point of the Arches is limited year-round. Summer-season (May 15 - Oct 15) quota permits are bulk-released April 15 at 7:00 am Pacific; no more availability opens later; itinerary changes are not allowed in quota areas except emergencies.

Nightly limits shown by recreation.gov's availability system (read 2026-10-08): Seafield Creek 6, North Side Ozette River 16, South Side Ozette River 12, Cape Alava 43, Wedding Rocks 20, South Sand Point 50, Yellow Banks 12; most other coastal camps show 100 permits (Shi Shi 100 permits/300 people) which may be a system cap rather than a managed quota.

Bear canisters are required for all food, garbage and scented items along the entire Wilderness Coast, overnight and whenever unattended; never hang food (raccoons). Canisters are loaned first-come at the Wilderness Information Center in Port Angeles; the Ozette Ranger Station does not loan or sell them.

Campfires: only on open beach below the high-tide line, at least 10 ft from drift logs, no more than 3 ft in diameter, driftwood only, never in forested sites; attend at all times and remove all traces. Fires in existing beach fire rings only near Rialto/Hole-in-the-Wall.
No campfires (or wood-burning stoves) at any time between the headland at Wedding Rocks and the headland north of Yellow Banks, including Sand Point and South Sand Point.
Fire bans override beach-fire rules: 2026 Stage 2 restrictions prohibited all campfires in the park from Aug 7 (stoves allowed if 3 ft from flammables); check status before each trip.
Maximum group size 12 (6 at Seafield Creek); associated groups larger than 12 must camp and travel at least 1 mile apart.
Pets, weapons, wheeled devices and stock are prohibited on coastal wilderness beaches and trails. Exception: leashed pets on Rialto Beach north to Ellen Creek in daylight (no camping with pets).
Leashed dogs are allowed on the frontcountry Kalaloch-area beaches such as Ruby Beach (WTA); confirm the exact Kalaloch pet zone with NPS.

No camping between the Quillayute River and Ellen Creek (Rialto Beach day-use zone); south of the Hoh River camping only in developed campgrounds (Kalaloch, South Beach); no camping on the Ozette Indian Reservation strip between Cape Alava and the South Side of Ozette River camp.
Tskawahyah (Cannonball) Island is always closed; offshore islands and sea stacks not reachable on foot at low tide are off-limits (national wildlife refuges).

Makah Recreation Pass ($20 per vehicle, valid the calendar year) is required to use Shi Shi Beach trail and other Makah Reservation sites; display in the windshield. No overnight parking at the Shi Shi trailhead.
Second Beach trailhead (Quileute Reservation) charges ~$10/day for parking (app or in person in La Push) as of summer 2026.

Use privies where available; otherwise dig catholes 6-8 in deep at least 200 ft (70 paces) from water, camps and trails; pack out toilet paper where there is no toilet; urinate on the beach below the high-tide line.
Do not build driftwood shelters or furniture; do not handle tide-pool animals or seal pups; you may take only a handful of unoccupied seashells.
Petroglyphs and archaeological sites are protected under the Archaeological Resources Protection Act; damaging them is a federal offense.
Do not touch metal cylinders or containers that wash ashore; note markings and location and report them to a ranger.

Carry a tide table and a watch and plan headland crossings for the 1-2 hours before low tide; never round a headland on an incoming tide. Check both daily lows (occasionally there is only one). Wind and storms can push water above predictions. Map symbols: 'Danger' = never passable on the beach; 'Caution' = passable below the stated tide height. Overland trails are marked by round red-and-black targets.
Plan short days: NPS says even strong hikers are usually limited to 5-10 miles per day on the coast because of tides, rock and sand.
Filter or boil all water (giardia and cryptosporidium present; iodine does not kill crypto). Tannin staining is normal.

conditions_2026.note: Mora Road (only road to Rialto Beach) closed to vehicles, bicycles and pedestrians beyond Mora Campground July 8 - Oct 15, 2026 for a permanent repair near milepost 1.25 (2019 flood damage). Mora Campground remains open. NPS suggests Ruby Beach or Kalaloch instead.

Recreation.gov lists Yellow Banks, Norwegian Memorial, Cedar Creek, Chilean Memorial and Hole-in-the-Wall as 'no access via Rialto 7/8-11/9', and Chilean Memorial and Hole-in-the-Wall show zero permit availability through Nov 9, 2026 (reopening Nov 10) - later than the NPS Oct 15 date. Other NPS versions said Oct 5 or Nov 9.

US 101 Hoh River Bridge (south of the Oil City Road turnoff): single-lane alternating traffic at 25 mph since July 14, 2026; nightly closures Sept 14-22 and full closures Sept 24-29, Oct 1-6 and Oct 8 (5 am) - Oct 13 (noon), 2026, with more closures promised; project July 2026 - Sept 2028. During full closures Ruby Beach, Kalaloch, Queets and Quinault are cut off from Forks (4+ hour detour via Hood Canal). Oil City and the Hoh Rain Forest stay reachable from Forks.

Hoko-Ozette Road open, paved, 21 mi from SR 112 (NPS road page entry dated 11/13/25). SR 112 has frequent closures and detours from flooding and landslides; SR 112 was repaved with pilot-car control in early August 2026.
Ozette area open; Ozette Campground open (primitive, first-come) but often closes in winter due to flooding.
Kalaloch: ranger station closed (passport stamps at the lodge); Kalaloch Campground open, reservations required May 15 - Sept 20, 2026; South Beach Campground first-come May 19 - Oct 10, 2026.

Campfires: park and forest Stage 2 restrictions banned all campfires from Aug 7, 2026 (still in effect in the Aug 26 release; USFS order ran through Oct 1). No rescission found as of Oct 8, 2026 - status unknown.
Scott's Bluff overland (South Coast): north-side ladder washed out, rope still in place (Apr-May 2026); rope up the south side improved. Rounding the bluff on the beach needed ~+1 ft or lower.
Hoh Head overland: several landslides took out tread above the bluffs; an NPS trail crew was rerouting and brushing in late April 2026; trail and ladders reported in great shape by mid-May 2026.

Taylor Point overland: 4-5 ladders all in great condition; newer stairs on the south descent; Scott Creek privy flagged closed in June 2026 but described as a 'nice covered privy' in Sept 2026; Toleak Point's south privy full (Sept 2026).

Point of the Arches to Seafield Creek: overland bluff routes badly eroded, ropes worn but secure, one rope ending ~25 ft above the beach (paracord extension) in June 2026; 'all in decent, passable condition' in July and late Aug 2026, with log obstacles and an eroding edge.

Shi Shi trail: first two-thirds in good shape with boardwalks; the muddy middle section remains deep (social trails around it); new stairs and a railing on the bluff descent; overnight parking $20/night cash (Aug 2026).

Ozette boardwalks: loose, rotten and missing boards with exposed nails (2026); a 10-ft section was removed on the Sand Point trail in April 2025 (possibly fixed). Trailhead flush toilets and water spigot working (July 2026).
Habituated black bear around Cape Alava camps (July 2026); sow with cubs at Sand Point (June 2026).
Whale carcasses on the beach at Toleak Point (two), near the Goodman Creek overland, Cape Alava, 0.5 mi south of the Ozette River and north of Seafield Creek during spring-summer 2026.
Second Beach trailhead lot closed for major improvements in April 2026; by July 2026 it was open, larger, and paid (~$10/day).

Cougar sighting notice at Third Beach trailhead; unofficial headland campsites near Scott Creek signed closed due to wildlife activity (June 2026). A burned trash pile was reported at Scott Creek (July 2026).

Norwegian Memorial: privy north of Norwegian Creek signed full; use the one south of the creek (June 2026). Cedar Creek privy shown on park map could not be found (May 2026). South Sand Point has a new privy (2025).
Recreation.gov showed Mosquito Creek with zero availability Oct 12-15, 2026 (cause not stated); daylight lows those days stayed above the 2 ft Diamond Rock limit.
Kalaloch Tree of Life dropped about 5 ft after early-2025 storms; the park will not intervene; 2026 status unconfirmed.

Tide calendar for game planning (NOAA predictions, La Push 9442396, 2026): lowest low -3.18 ft on Jun 16 at 08:15; highest high 11.0 ft on Dec 24. Days per month with a daylight (06:00-19:59) low at or below 2 ft: Jan 20, Feb 25, Mar 31, Apr 30, May 28, Jun 22, Jul 21, Aug 19, Sep 13, Oct 9, Nov 14, Dec 15. Summer minus tides fall in the morning; Oct-Feb minus tides fall in the evening or night. Example Oct 7-16, 2026: morning lows +0.2 to +4.3 ft, evening lows +1.8 to -0.6 ft, highs 6.3-9.3 ft.
Wildfire smoke reached the coast in August 2026 (hikers 'smoked out' of trips elsewhere sought the coast).

uncertain_claims: Mora Road reopening date conflicts: NPS conditions/road pages say Oct 15, 2026; recreation.gov camp names and availability say Nov 9, 2026; an earlier NPS version said Oct 5.
Campfire ban status as of Oct 2026 unknown (Stage 2 from Aug 7; USFS order ran to Oct 1; no rescission notice found).

Beach segment mileages on the North Coast between named camps are reconstructed from NPS totals (20 mi Ozette-Rialto; 15 mi Shi Shi-Ozette), the NPS tidal-restriction mile marks, Oregon Hikers' mile log, WTA (Chilean Memorial 3.7 mi from Rialto) and straight-line coordinate distances; individual legs could be off by 0.3-0.5 mi. Norwegian Memorial to Cedar Creek is especially uncertain (1.0-2.0 mi).

Point of the Arches to Seafield Creek (3.7 mi) and the three overland trail lengths (0.4, 0.7, 0.1 mi) come from June-July 2026 trip reports, not NPS; gain/loss there are estimates (~250 ft bluffs) or null.

Tide limits not published by NPS but reported by hikers: Scott's Bluff beach rounding ~+1 ft; pinch 0.5 mi north of the Ozette River ~6 ft (Custom Correct map via trip report); the Cape Alava-Sand Point pinch points; Hole-in-the-Wall arch passage height.
Which named headland sits at each NPS tidal mile mark (e.g., 2.4 mi and 5.1 mi north of Rialto, 4.9 and 7.9 mi south of Ozette) is inferred from trip reports and maps.
Recreation.gov availability totals of 100 (and 300 people at Shi Shi) may be system caps rather than true quotas; Sand Point's 100 may or may not be a real limit.
Hole-in-the-Wall camp location: NPS Rialto page puts camps between Ellen Creek and the arch; the NPS camp KML point lies just north of the arch.

Toilet presence conflicts: Scott Creek (NPS route page: no privy; camp map and 2026 reports: privy), Cedar Creek (NPS list: yes; KML and 2026 hikers: none found), Seafield Creek (KML: no; one 2026 report mentions a privy).
Willoughby Creek (water and privy listed for Shi Shi) could not be located precisely; omitted as a node.
Shi Shi overnight parking price: $10/day (WTA, older blogs) vs $20/night (Aug 2026 reports); private lot rules can change.
Ozette trailhead parking fee amount for visitors without a pass was not found.
Mosquito Creek showing zero availability Oct 12-15, 2026 is unexplained; the Diamond Rock tide window is a guess.
Elevations are USGS 3DEP point samples at node coordinates (beach and cliff nodes can read high or low); Goodman Creek ford position and elevation approximate.
Drive minutes are OSRM estimates and do not account for 2026 closures (Mora Road, Hoh River Bridge) or pilot-car delays.
Ericson's Bay trail length: NPS GIS 1.86 mi; Wikipedia 2.5 mi; trip report 'two miles'.
Allen's Bay abandoned route from Lake Ozette to Norwegian Memorial / Kayostla Beach exists but is overgrown (Aug 2025 report); not included as a segment.
Kalaloch Tree of Life 2026 condition unconfirmed; coordinates not taken from an authoritative source.
No reservation system for Shi Shi overnight parking was found; it is a private cash lot (the task brief mentioned 'reservation parking').
Oil City Road leaving US 101 north of the Hoh River Bridge (so unaffected by 2026 bridge closures) is inferred from WTA directions (MP 177-178, 'just north of the Hoh River').
Yellow sand verbena on Olympic wilderness beaches is unverified; listed only as a candidate 'golden glow' plant.
Second Beach parking fee amount and payment method (app/in-store) come from 2026 trip reports, not an official Quileute source.
Whale-death count (31 in Washington by Aug 2026) is a trip-report claim, not verified with NOAA.

Several NPS coast pages (tides-and-your-safety 2023, Ozette 2025, Shi Shi 2025, Oil City 2025, Third Beach 2025) were last updated before or during 2025; core rules are stable but details may be stale.
